# Senate Finance Committee Hearing Prep
## Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act
### Witness Prep Materials — Democratic Members

---

## Ron Wyden (D-OR, Ranking Member)

**Line 1 — IRS Funding and Service Levels**
Wyden has consistently tied taxpayer service quality to IRS appropriations. He will likely press on whether the bill's service provisions are adequately funded and whether any funding mechanisms are vulnerable to rescission or offsetting cuts under concurrent budget negotiations.

**Line 2 — Free Filing and Private Preparer Conflicts**
Wyden has been a long-standing critic of the paid preparer lobby's influence on IRS free-file programs. He will likely ask whether the bill strengthens, weakens, or is silent on direct free-file options, and whether Treasury has assessed taxpayer cost burdens under current preparer-dominated channels.

**Suggested Response Posture**
Affirm shared commitment to service-level improvements. Cite specific provisions in the bill that expand or protect direct taxpayer access. Offer to provide a written breakdown of funding assumptions tied to each service enhancement. Avoid being drawn into broader IRS appropriations debates outside the bill's scope.

---

## Maria Cantwell (D-WA)

**Line 1 — Technology Modernization**
Cantwell has prioritized IRS technology infrastructure. She will likely ask whether the bill includes enforceable timelines and accountability mechanisms for IT system modernization, and whether legacy system failures are addressed in the service provisions.

**Line 2 — Small Business and Gig Economy Filers**
Washington state has a significant gig economy workforce. She will likely press on whether the bill addresses complexity and compliance burdens for self-employed and platform-economy workers, including 1099-K reporting thresholds.

**Suggested Response Posture**
Acknowledge the technology modernization challenge directly. Reference any bill provisions tied to system upgrades. On gig economy filers, note Treasury's ongoing regulatory work on 1099-K thresholds and express willingness to work with the committee on further statutory clarity if warranted.

---

## Michael F. Bennet (D-CO)

**Line 1 — Rural and Underserved Taxpayer Access**
Bennet has focused on service equity for rural Coloradans. He will likely ask whether the bill expands in-person or hybrid taxpayer assistance in rural and frontier communities, and whether Taxpayer Assistance Centers are included in any service expansion.

**Line 2 — Child Tax Credit Administration**
Bennet has been a leading advocate for expanding the Child Tax Credit. He will likely probe whether the bill improves IRS administrative capacity to process refundable credits accurately and quickly, and whether it reduces erroneous denial rates for low-income claimants.

**Suggested Response Posture**
Reference any rural access provisions directly. On the Child Tax Credit, affirm Treasury's administrative commitment to accurate and timely refundable credit processing. If the bill does not directly address CTC expansion, note that the bill's service improvements benefit all filer categories including low-income families.

---

## Mark R. Warner (D-VA)

**Line 1 — Cybersecurity and Data Protection**
Warner chairs or participates in intelligence-adjacent oversight and has focused on federal data security. He will likely ask what cybersecurity standards govern taxpayer data under the bill and whether the legislation strengthens IRS systems against foreign adversary intrusion.

**Line 2 — Workforce and Contractor Oversight**
Virginia's large federal contractor workforce means Warner pays attention to IRS staffing models. He will likely ask whether the bill addresses hiring, retention, and contractor accountability for the IRS workforce delivering the expanded services contemplated.

**Suggested Response Posture**
Address cybersecurity by referencing IRS compliance with FISMA requirements and any bill provisions touching data protection. On workforce, cite Treasury's position on IRS staffing plans under current appropriations. Offer to provide a written supplement on contractor oversight frameworks if pressed.

---

## Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI)

**Line 1 — Wealthy Taxpayer Audit Enforcement**
Whitehouse has consistently argued that IRS service improvements must be paired with robust enforcement targeting high-income noncompliance. He will likely ask whether the bill contains any provisions that could constrain IRS audit capacity for high-wealth filers or pass-through entities.

**Line 2 — Dark Money and Tax-Exempt Abuse**
Whitehouse has focused on 501(c)(4) and related exempt organization oversight. He will likely ask whether the bill includes any provisions affecting IRS oversight of tax-exempt organizations and whether enforcement resources for that function are protected.

**Suggested Response Posture**
Affirm that service and enforcement are complementary functions and that nothing in the bill reduces enforcement capacity. Acknowledge the committee's interest in high-wealth compliance and note Treasury's administrative initiatives in that area. On exempt organizations, distinguish between administrative service improvements and enforcement functions and clarify that both are sustained.

---

## Margaret Wood Hassan (D-NH)

**Line 1 — Taxpayer Rights and Dispute Resolution**
Hassan has focused on constituent service and administrative fairness. She will likely ask whether the bill strengthens taxpayer rights in the dispute resolution process, including access to the Taxpayer Advocate Service and timeliness of responses to taxpayer correspondence.

**Line 2 — Small Business Compliance Burden**
New Hampshire has a high concentration of small businesses. She will likely press on whether the bill reduces paperwork and compliance complexity for small business owners and whether any provisions inadvertently increase their reporting obligations.

**Suggested Response Posture**
Reference specific bill provisions that address correspondence backlogs and Taxpayer Advocate capacity. On small business burden, affirm Treasury's commitment to regulatory simplification and note any provisions in the bill directed at reducing small business compliance costs. Offer specific examples if available.

---

## Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV)

**Line 1 — Consumer Protection for Vulnerable Filers**
Cortez Masto's consumer protection focus will likely lead her to ask whether the bill includes safeguards against predatory tax preparers, including preparer credentials, fee disclosure requirements, or referral to IRS oversight programs such as the Annual Filing Season Program.

**Line 2 — Nevada-Specific Equity: Hospitality and Tip Workers**
Nevada's economy depends heavily on hospitality workers who receive tip income. She will likely ask whether the bill improves IRS guidance and administrative processes for tip income reporting, and whether it reduces compliance friction or audit risk for low- and moderate-income tipped workers.

**Suggested Response Posture**

bills.nexus: H.Con.Res. 113 sets the discretionary and mandatory spending ceilings and revenue floors that directly constrain Treasury's debt management operations and the Office of Tax Policy's projections for fiscal years 2027 through 2036. Treasury's Office of Fiscal Affairs and the Fiscal Assistant Secretary must align financing schedules and borrowing authority with whatever aggregate deficit path the resolution locks in, creating execution risk if enacted levels diverge sharply from current baseline assumptions.

bills.title: A bill to name the community-based outpatient clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs in Newton, New Jersey, as the "Anthony 'Tony' J. Gallopo VA Clinic".
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
bills.nexus: Treasury has no jurisdictional interest in S. 5100, as it touches only VA facility naming authority under the Department of Veterans Affairs, with no tax, fiscal, financial regulatory, or appropriations implications for Treasury. No implementation burden or financial risk accrues to any Treasury office.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to apply inflation adjustments to the additional hospital insurance tax on high income taxpayers.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5085 would amend IRC Section 1401(b)(2) to index the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax thresholds for inflation, directly implicating IRS's administration of payroll and self-employment tax withholding. Treasury and IRS would face implementation burden in updating threshold tables, revising Form 8959 instructions, and coordinating with employers on withholding adjustments each year.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to apply inflation adjustments to the base amount and adjusted base amount for purposes of determining taxable social security benefits.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5084 directly affects IRS because it amends the Internal Revenue Code to index the income thresholds at which Social Security benefits become taxable, provisions that have remained unadjusted since 1983. Treasury's Office of Tax Policy would need to score the revenue loss and coordinate with SSA on implementation, while IRS would face system and form updates to reflect the new inflation-adjusted base amounts.

bills.title: Fair Treatment of Religious Organizations Act of 2026
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 23 - 16.
bills.nexus: Without a known nexus provided and based solely on the bill title, Treasury's interest is limited unless the bill touches tax-exempt status rules under IRC Section 501(c)(3), which falls under IRS jurisdiction within Treasury. If the bill modifies eligibility, restrictions, or enforcement standards for religious organizations' tax-exempt status, IRS would face implementation demands around compliance determinations and potential revenue impact.

bills.title: Stop CHEATERS Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Appropriations.
bills.nexus:
I don't have reliable details on H.R. 9736 "Stop CHEATERS Act" in my training data, so I cannot provide accurate, factual sentences without risking misinformation.

Could you share the bill's known nexus, key provisions, or a summary? With that, I can give you a precise two-sentence brief for the Legislative Affairs team.

bills.title: Biomass Facility Construction Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9746 likely proposes new or expanded tax credits or incentives for biomass facility construction, placing it squarely within the jurisdiction of the Office of Tax Policy and the Internal Revenue Service. Treasury's implementation concern centers on designing and administering any credit mechanism to prevent improper claims while ensuring the incentive achieves its intended energy policy outcome.

bills.title: To name the Department of Veterans Affairs community-based outpatient clinic in Newton, New Jersey, as the "Anthony "Tony" J. Gallopo VA Clinic".
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
bills.nexus: This bill solely involves the Department of Veterans Affairs and carries no Treasury jurisdiction, appropriations impact, or financial regulatory implications. No Treasury office or authority is touched, and there is no implementation burden or fiscal risk for the Department to monitor.

bills.title: To designate the community-based outpatient clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs in Lafayette, Louisiana, as the "Rodney C. Hamilton Sr. VA Clinic".
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
bills.nexus: This bill has no direct nexus to Treasury, as it solely directs the Department of Veterans Affairs to rename a Louisiana outpatient clinic and confers no tax, appropriations, debt, or financial regulatory implications. No Treasury office or authority is implicated, and the bill presents zero implementation burden or fiscal risk for the Department.

bills.title: To name the Department of Veterans Affairs community-based outpatient clinic in San Jose, California, as the "Corporal Patrick D. Tillman VA Clinic".
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 4288 is a VA facility-naming bill that falls solely under the jurisdiction of the Department of Veterans Affairs, not Treasury, and involves no tax, fiscal, or financial regulatory authority. Treasury has no implementation role or material risk exposure from this legislation.

bills.title: Protecting Innocent Taxpayers from Endless Assessments Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 4964 directly implicates IRS assessment authority under Title 26, placing it squarely within the purview of the IRS Office of Chief Counsel and the Tax Legislative Counsel at Treasury. The bill's limitations on assessment timelines create revenue risk and could constrain IRS enforcement capacity, requiring Treasury to evaluate fiscal exposure and potential regulatory responses.

bills.title: Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agency Appropriations Act, 2027
bills.nexus: Treasury has limited direct equities in this bill, as it primarily funds USDA, FDA, and rural development programs outside Treasury's core jurisdiction; however, the Office of Management and Budget and Treasury's debt management functions have an interest in the overall discretionary spending levels and any rescissions or borrowing authority provisions embedded in the measure. Implementation risk centers on whether the bill contains any commodity credit, rural lending, or food assistance financing mechanisms that interact with Treasury's debt issuance or Federal Financing Bank obligations.

bills.title: Workforce Housing Tax Credit Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8626 would establish a new tax credit administered through the Internal Revenue Code, directly implicating IRS and the Office of Tax Policy in designing eligibility rules, credit calculations, and compliance mechanisms. The primary risk is revenue cost and the administrative burden of standing up a new credit program, including potential for improper claims if program rules are not tightly drafted before enactment.

bills.title: Stop CHEATERS Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 4298 targets fraudulent claims for tax credits and deductions, placing it squarely within IRS enforcement authority and the Treasury's tax expenditure oversight role. Treasury's implementation concern centers on the administrative burden and resource requirements the IRS would face in expanding fraud-detection and audit capacity under the bill's provisions.

bills.title: GENIUS Act
bills.nexus: The GENIUS Act establishes a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, directly implicating Treasury's Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Financial Stability Oversight Council, both of which receive new or clarified authority under the law. Treasury must implement issuer licensing standards, anti-money laundering compliance requirements, and foreign issuer restrictions, creating significant rulemaking and enforcement obligations while managing systemic risk exposure from dollar-denominated stablecoin markets.
